metaDescription: Seven propane gas grills under $300 compared on burners, grate material, cooking area, side burner and build, with the trade-offs this budget forces.
expertTake: The Char-Broil Performance Series is our top pick under $300 because four burners, a side burner and a griddle upgrade option give a family room to grow. The Nexgrill 562 square inch model is the pick for hosts who want cast iron grates and the largest area in the known brands. Skip this price band if you want thick gauge steel, a long burner warranty or a searing system, because those start above $300.
introParagraphs: A propane gas grill under $300 gets you four burners, a side burner and a lid on a cart. What it does not get you is heavy gauge steel, a ten year burner warranty or a lid that holds heat like a premium cabinet. The grills in this band cook well when you learn their hot spots, and they fail first in the places the cap economizes on: thin lids, thin firebox sheet and burners that rust.

So the buying question is which compromises you accept. BTU numbers climb as the listing gets more aggressive, but they say little about even heat. Listing prices move, so the $300 cap reflects Amazon prices when this guide was updated. We evaluated these grills from spec sheets, listing details and owner feedback patterns, and none of it replaces the maker's safety instructions.

products.name: AMERLIFE 6 burner propane grill, 60,000 BTU, 650 sq in, side burner

specList.label: Burners
specList.value: 6 main at 8,000 BTU, 1 side at 12,000 BTU

products.description:
The AMERLIFE is the largest grill here, with six 8,000 BTU main burners, a 12,000 BTU side burner and a listed 650 square inches of cooking area including a warming rack. The grates are cast iron, which hold heat well for searing, and the cabinet includes storage space for a propane tank and tools.

The tradeoff is that big numbers at this price usually mean thinner materials. The listing leans on BTU and area, not on gauge or warranty, so treat it as a big, cheap grill, not a durable one. Against the Char-Broil Performance, you get two more burners and more area, but less documentation. Against the Nexgrill, it has more area and a similar grate, at a higher tier. Six burners give you zones, but only if you learn to manage them, since cheap burners can run uneven.

Budget for a cover, since thin painted or stainless panels rust where moisture sits. Clean the grates after every cook, empty the grease tray often and check hose connections with soapy water before each season. Expect to replace burners sooner than on premium grills, and keep the model number for parts.

products.name: Bestfire 5 burner propane grill, 68,000 BTU total, 447 sq in grates, side burner

specList.label: Cooking area
specList.value: 447 sq in grates plus 200 sq in warming rack

specList.label: Best for
specList.value: Cooking for a crowd on a budget

products.description:
The Bestfire lists five main burners plus a side burner at 68,000 BTU total, with 447 square inches of porcelain enameled grates and a 200 square inch warming rack. It uses a standard 20 pound propane tank, a push button ignition and a removable grease tray, and the listing suggests it can hold more than 40 burgers or 8 racks of ribs at once.

The porcelain enamel grates are easier to clean than bare cast iron but chip over the years, exposing metal that can rust. A BTU total of 68,000 is the highest here, but BTU measures fuel input, not heat on the food, so judge it on how evenly the five burners spread flame. Against the AMERLIFE, it has fewer burners and less area. Against the Char-Broil Performance, it offers more burners at a similar tier but a less established brand.

Keep the lid down when preheating and let the grates reach temperature before the first cook. Clean the grease tray every few cooks and replace the grates if the enamel chips. Check the hose and regulator for cracks at the start of each season and always light with the lid open.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Under $300 you get four to six burners, a side burner and a lid on a cart, usually in painted or thin stainless steel. You do not get thick castings, a ten year burner warranty or a searing station. The Char-Broil Performance and Monument Mesa are the more considered builds here, while the AMERLIFE and Bestfire push area and BTU. Decide whether you want a durable small grill or a big cheap one.

BTU is fuel input, not heat on the food. The Bestfire lists 68,000 BTU total, the AMERLIFE 60,000, the Nexgrill 52,000 and the Char-Broil Classic 30,000, but a well built 30,000 BTU grill can cook as well as a leaky 60,000 one. Look at burner count, burner material and burner warranty. Stainless burners, like the 304 stainless on the Monument Mesa, last longer than aluminized steel.

Cast iron, as on the Nexgrill, AMERLIFE and IdeaMaxx, holds heat for searing but needs oiling to avoid rust. Porcelain enamel, as on the Char-Broil Classic and Bestfire, cleans easier but can chip. Stainless rods are the middle path. Cast iron wins for steaks, and porcelain wins for convenience.

The Nexgrill lists 562 square inches, the AMERLIFE 650, the Char-Broil Classic 360 and the IdeaMaxx 302. More area feeds a crowd but demands more patio space and a bigger cover. Measure the patio before you buy, and remember that area listed with a warming rack overstates the usable searing surface.

A thin lid and firebox lose heat in wind and cold weather, which forces the burners to run higher. Look for a double wall or thick lid, a tight lid seam and a heat gauge that reads in the lid. Budget grills often skimp here, which is why they are slower to preheat. A heavy lid is the quickest guide in the store, but not on a listing.

Do not give up a reliable ignition, good burners or a lid that closes tightly to save a small amount. It is fine to give up a side burner, a built in thermometer and storage doors. Plan to buy a cover, since rust is the main reason a grill at this price dies early.

howWeEvaluated.title: Burners and output
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared burner count and listed BTU, treating BTU as a fuel figure. The AMERLIFE has six main burners and the Char-Broil Classic has three. We weighted burner material over raw BTU.

howWeEvaluated.title: Grates and area
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at grate material and the usable area. The Nexgrill lists 562 square inches of cast iron, and the Bestfire lists 447 square inches of porcelain. We discounted warming racks.

howWeEvaluated.title: Build and warranty
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked steel and warranty details. The Char-Broil Performance lists a 2 year warranty and the Monument Mesa lists 304 stainless burners. A listing with no build detail ranked lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Extras and setup
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed side burners, storage and assembly time. The Monument Mesa lists about 30 minutes of assembly and the Char-Broil Performance offers a griddle upgrade option. Foldable shelves on the IdeaMaxx earn credit for portability.

howWeEvaluated.title: Budget fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We kept only listings at or below the cap and used price tiers for ordering. All of this rests on spec sheets, listing details and owner feedback patterns, not lab measurement.

cards.label: Cast iron
cards.text: The Nexgrill, AMERLIFE and IdeaMaxx use cast iron. It holds heat and sears well, but needs oiling and regular care to avoid rust.

cards.label: Porcelain
cards.text: The Char-Broil Classic and Bestfire use porcelain. It cleans easily and resists rust at first, but chips can expose the metal.

howToChoose.note: Choose cast iron if you sear often, and porcelain if you want low effort cleaning.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Four burners, a tight lid, a reliable ignition and a grate you will clean. Plan on a cover and a replacement burner over time.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Char-Broil Performance is the balanced pick, and the Monument Mesa leans toward stainless burners and searing.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want thicker steel, a long burner warranty, an infrared searing system or a grill you plan to keep for ten years. Those start above this cap.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You cook a few times a week and accept replacing burners or the cover. The grills here cover that need.

faq.q: Is a $300 gas grill any good?
faq.a: Yes, if you accept thinner steel and a shorter warranty. The cooking is fine once you learn the hot spots. These grills fail first in burners, lids and rust, so a cover and care matter.

faq.q: Does more BTU mean a hotter grill?
faq.a: No. BTU is fuel input. Burner count, material and lid fit matter more. A well built 30,000 BTU grill can outcook a leaky 60,000 BTU one.

faq.q: What do I give up versus a pricier grill?
faq.a: Expect thinner steel, shorter warranties and fewer premium touches such as infrared burners or thick castings. You keep four or more burners and a side burner.
Cast iron sears better but needs oiling. Porcelain is easier to clean but can chip. Choose by how you cook.

faq.q: How do I check for gas leaks?
faq.a: Brush soapy water on the hose and fittings with the gas on and look for bubbles. Do this at the start of every season and after moving the tank, and follow the maker's manual.
